title: fix(mcp): validate_expression gives the runtime publish gate's verdict at a flow condition and judges the field being authored
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoSLDKWQ8v7cxY9uDGijfncD)_

Fixes #33147

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the MCP `validate_expression` tool now answers `ok: false` (or a warning) at a `flow_condition`, and for a named stored or formula field at a `formula` site, where the publish gate already refuses (or warns). It also accepts two new optional inputs, `startCondition` and `field`, which is the widening arm. The gate's acceptance set does not change.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — the published skills say only that the tool runs the build's validator, which stays true; what it judges at each site is taught by the served `SKILL.md` line this diff updates (and its Console mirror, byte for byte).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:MCP `validate_expression` 在 `flow_condition` 位点按运行时发布门禁对流程写入的判法,跑门禁自己的检查(记录触发流程上 `record.`/`previous.` 未判空的可空字段报错,外部对象未落存储的系统列告警);新增两个可选入参:`startCondition`(下游条件继承起始条件已证的非空)和 `field`(公式位点按该字段本身判:存储字段给存储表达式告警,公式字段给循环判定)。
- 为什么改:工具承诺给出发布门禁的判定,但在流程条件上只跑共享校验器,门禁拒的条件它答 `ok: true`,代理到保存流程时才第一次被拒;存储字段的告警和公式循环它也答不出。
- 风险与回滚:只收窄一个建议性工具的判定,门禁接受集不变,门禁接受的表达式答案与之前逐字相同;两个新入参可选,旧调用不受影响。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts`(流程探针与 `field` 就地替换)、`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` 的 `validate_expression` 入参与 `gatePassFindings`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/authored-site-expression.test.ts`,预期 50 个测试全过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

PR #33134 closed the gap at the `validation` and `formula` sites. This PR closes the three gaps it left.

**1. `flow_condition`: the gate's own passes.** Measured at the #33134 head (`fbdba070`) before this change, on a record-triggered flow on `task` with `days` nullable. Each condition was placed on the start node, a `decision` branch and an edge, and all three slots answered alike:

| condition | `os validate` (build door) | runtime flow publish door | tool before | tool after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `record.days > 3` | error | error | ok | error, gate's sentence |
| `previous.days > 3` | error | error | ok | error, gate's sentence |
| `record.owner_id == 'u1'` on an external object | warning | warning | none | warning, gate's sentence |
| `days > 3` (bare) | error | silent | ok | ok, as that door |
| `user.id == 'u1'`, `foo.bar == 1` | error (unbound root) | silent | ok | ok, as that door |
| `record.title == 'x'` (CONTROL) | silent | silent | ok | ok, unchanged |

The two doors disagree because the runtime publish gate's per-write snapshot shows no entrance, so its root scope is never provable (`perWriteSnapshotEntrance`). That turns off the bare-name null guard and the unbound-root refusal there. The existing pin in `validate-expressions.flow-null-guards.test.ts` already records this disagreement.

The seat chose the **runtime flow publish door**, the one a flow saved through MCP or Studio meets. The tool must never refuse what that door accepts. So `ok` at a `flow_condition` is that door's verdict, not `os validate`'s. The tool description, the served `SKILL.md` line and the changeset each say this in one sentence and tell an agent to write `record.FIELD`.

- `@objectstack/lint` `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` takes `site: 'flow_condition'`. ⛔ It still re-implements no pass. It builds a one-flow probe (`authoredFlowProbe`): a start node bound to `objectName` with the trigger the caller names, its start condition when one is given, and one edge to an end node carrying the condition. It then runs the gate's own walk with `runtimeWriteType: 'flow'` and keeps the findings on that edge's key path (`flows[0].edges[0].condition`). Each trigger kind is spelled the way `resolveFlowTriggerKind` reads it, and a pin reads every kind back.
- The whole entry is now one `runStackExpressionPasses` call. Only the stack, the write type and the slot filter differ by site. `sharedValidatorRunByCaller` still has one passer, and the source pin from #33134 still holds that.
- `@objectstack/mcp`: `VALIDATE_SITE_MAP.flow_condition` gains `gatePasses: 'flow_condition'`. At a flow condition the tool reads the subject's served definition and nothing else, because nothing hydrates a relationship hop there.

**2. New optional input `startCondition`** (site `flow_condition` only). The gate presumes what a flow's start condition proves at every condition downstream. Without that presumption, the tool would refuse `record.days > 3` on an edge after a start condition `record.days != null`, which the gate accepts. Given `startCondition`, the probe carries it on the start node, and the gate's own presumption applies. That includes the door split for a bare start guard: `days != null` proves nothing at the runtime door, so the edge is still refused there and here. Omitted, the condition is judged as the start condition itself. A pin shows that a start probe and an edge probe answer alike when no start condition is given, so no slot input is needed.

**3. New optional input `field`** (site `formula` only, a snake_case field name): the field the expression is authored on. It resolves only through the caller's served definition (`servedObjectDefinitionOf`).
- A declared field keeps its definition with the expression in place. A stored field (any type but `formula`) then gets the gate's `storedExpressionInputIssues` warnings (card item 2), and a formula field is judged on the object's formula graph under its own name, so `formulaCycleIssues` refuses the cycle it would close (card item 3).
- Any other name, including a field masked from the caller, is judged as a new formula field of that name. So the answer never says whether a hidden field exists, and a pin holds a masked field and an absent one to the same answer.

Other surfaces:
- The tool description and the served `SKILL.md` line, with its Console mirror byte for byte, name what is judged at a `flow_condition`, the two inputs, and the limits.
- `startCondition` on another site and `field` on another site are refused, like the existing site-scoped inputs.
- Changeset `.changeset/33147-validate-expression-flow-condition-parity.md`: patch for `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/lint` and `@object-ui/console`, with the **BREAKING** verdict-narrowing banner and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition, naming both inputs.

## Tests

- `packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.test.ts` (26 → 50 tests)
  - **Flow enumeration pin.** Every call the gate makes at a flow condition is classified, read off the gate's source through the shared comment mask. The regions are the start node's condition block, the `decision` branch block, the edge block, and the `check` / `checkDeclaredPredicate` helpers they hand the source to. Bare calls and member calls are both covered. The classification:
    - `checkFlowNullGuards` and `warnUnprovisionedAnchors` are `pass`. Each is pinned at all three slots: the entry's findings equal the runtime gate's on a hand-written flow (start, `decision`, two ends, three edges).
    - `refuseUnboundRoots` and `warnShadowedFieldReads` are `pass-silent-here`, with the reason: os validate's whole-flow judgments over variables, node ids and entrances. Each pin is non-vacuous: `os validate` speaks on the same condition, given the bindings it reads.
    - `refuseStoredMetadataBodyHop` and `refuseUndeclaredHopField` are `pass-silent-here`: they run only where a hop is hydrated.
    - The bare-name null guard has its own pin: `os validate` refuses it, and the runtime gate and the entry do not.
    - `validateExpression`, `checkStructuralCondition` and `predicateSlotRefusal` are the validator and envelope checks the tool runs itself. The rest is plumbing.
  - **startCondition.** A guarded edge passes and a guarded `decision` passes. A bare start guard still refuses, as at the runtime door. The start condition's own findings are not reported.
  - **Trigger kinds.** Every kind reads back through `resolveFlowTriggerKind`, and each answers as the gate does. The null guard fires on a record-triggered flow only.
  - **CONTROL**, a served definition with injected columns judged as the authored body, the object's own rules ignored, and an absent object answering `[]`.
  - **`field`.** A declared stored field gets the gate's stored-expression warnings, and the unnamed probe gets none. A declared formula gets the cycle refusal under its own name. Array-form fields read the same. An undeclared name answers like no name.
  - The #33134 rows are unchanged. The `formulaCycleIssues` and `storedExpressionInputIssues` classifications keep `pass-silent-here` for the unnamed probe, and their reasons now point at the `field` block.
- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-validate-expression.test.ts` (60 → 72 tests)
  - Tool-level members at `flow_condition`: the `record.` null guard, the `previous.` null guard, and the anchor warning. Each is the gate's verdict and sentence, and the definition-less bridge answered ok before.
  - A bare `days > 3` answers exactly as before. A start guard is honoured. A schedule flow gets no null guard. CONTROL equals the definition-less bridge.
  - The subject is the only definition read at a flow condition. The #33134 pin that said `flow_condition` reads nothing now covers `template` alone.
  - A `field` block with a masking bridge. A stored field's warnings, the cycle refusal, and **a field masked from the caller answers exactly as a field the object does not declare** (and as no field at all). A bad field name is refused.
  - The refusal table gains the five site-scoped refusals of the two inputs.

## Acceptance notes

- **`ok` at a `flow_condition` is the runtime publish gate's verdict, not `os validate`'s.** `os validate` also refuses a bare name's unguarded null read, a root the run does not bind, and warns on a read a flow variable shadows. It judges those over the whole flow's variables, node ids and entrances, which the tool is not handed. The runtime door gives none of them, and the tool follows it so that it never refuses a condition that door accepts.
- **The probe's names.** A gate sentence that names the slot names it `flow 'this flow' · edge 'this condition' (start→end) condition`, because the tool is handed the condition and not the flow it will sit in.
- **A new stored field gets no stored-expression warnings until it is declared.** An undeclared `field` is judged as a new formula field, and there is no `fieldType` input (seat ruling). Once the field is declared, or served in a draft, it is judged as stored.
- **The masked-field guarantee rests on the served definition.** `field` resolves only through `servedObjectDefinitionOf`, and the runtime bridge serves that through `readObjectForCaller`, which masks a field the caller cannot read. `mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts`'s case table already pins that mask from #33134. This PR adds the tool-level pin that a masked name and an absent name answer alike.
- **A `decision` branch and an edge are the same slot to the gate**, apart from the start-condition presumption, so there is no slot input. A non-start node's `config.condition` is inert and the gate does not judge it.
- **Ruling grep** (`ruling|Ruling-ref|maintainer|⛔`) before editing, on the surface: `authored-site-expression.ts` 1 (its own ⛔ no re-implementation), `validate-expressions.ts` 28, `lint/src/index.ts` 7, `mcp-http-tools.ts` 39, `skill-md.ts` 1. The ones that bear on this change are the root-scope stand-down at the runtime gate (rulings `5791822697` item 3 and `6104584601`, cited in `flow-cel-root-scope.ts`). This PR follows them: the tool judges no root where that door judges none.
- **Writes:** relay writes and MCP calls are counted in the `os-dev-report` comment.

## Verification

      -> 4 failed | 46 passed (50): refuseUnboundRoots silent-here, the bare-name null guard pin, the start-condition pin (bare guard), the trigger-kind pin

      -> 2 failed | 48 passed (50): stored-field warnings, array-form fields

      -> 1 failed | 49 passed (50): "presumes what the start condition proves" (the start condition's own finding leaked)

L4b gate: a new call refuseSomethingNew(...) in the edge block of validate-expressions.ts
      -> "every call the gate makes at a flow condition is classified" red (+ "refuseSomethingNew"); the undefined call also throws at run time, so the other flow pins red with it
